assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators opened a new classification of quantum states of matter, with helical edge states protected by symmetry. It is original, conceptually clean and has strongly shaped materials physics and electronic-structure theory (topological invariants computed from first principles). It fits the committee's recent interest in topological and quantum phases and is a natural complement to the 2016 prize.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall proposal in graphene. Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental demonstration in HgTe quantum wells, following a prediction by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang who are not in the credited names. Theory-plus-experiment trio is a fair configuration, but the omission of the HgTe prediction and the independent 3D TI work is a recognized allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups (HgTe, InAs/GaSb, Bi-based 3D materials, ARPES and transport) and by quantitative DFT predictions matching measured spectra. Mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe quantum spin Hall prediction (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and 3D topological insulators (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore, Balents; Hasan, Zhang groups) is outside the supplied credit set.
Quantized edge conductance in the original experiments was imperfect; I rely on memory of the literature and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A flat-band, strongly correlated system tunable by twist angle produced superconductivity, correlated insulators and orbital magnetism in a simple carbon platform. It is a surprising new quantum behaviour in a material that theorists had assumed to be an uncomplicated weakly correlated system, and it has launched the moire materials field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle with a continuum model; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experiments, with Yuan Cao as first author who is not credited. The theory-experiment pairing is clean, though the experimental credit is partly shared with the student and with contemporaneous groups.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups across twisted multilayers and TMD moire systems, but the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is unsettled and the field is still evolving, so timing is slightly early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and the full phase diagram remain debated; sample-to-sample variation (strain, disorder) is large.
Whether the committee will wait for the interpretation to stabilize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Iron-pnictide superconductors were the first high-Tc family beyond cuprates, reaching 55 K with a clearly multiband magnetic-fluctuation context. The discovery was unexpected because iron magnetism was thought to be inimical to superconductivity, which is exactly the sort of experiment-overturns-theory case that matters to me.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the first report (LaFeAsO with F doping, 2008). Chen's and Zhao's groups quickly raised Tc to 43-55 K in rare-earth variants. Hosono is the clear originator; whether the Chinese contributions warrant co-recognition is a genuine allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed, with large theoretical literature including DFT and spin-fluctuation pictures; however, the pairing mechanism remains unresolved and the practical Tc ceiling has not risen.
uncertainties: Whether Chen and Zhao should share credit or Hosono alone is cited for the foundational step.
Pairing mechanism unresolved; DFT predicts magnetic moments poorly in some compounds.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proposals for quantum computing with trapped ions and for quantum simulation with cold atoms and ions defined the architecture for two experimental platforms and underpin the field of programmable quantum simulators. The work is original and lasting; it is a theory prize that rests on spectacular experimental realizations.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are clearly the central pair, with the 1995 trapped-ion gate proposal and the 1998 Hubbard-in-optical-lattices proposal with Jaksch et al. A two-person prize is clean, though experimental laureates of the 2012 prize already honoured part of the ion field.
assessment.maturity: Strongly validated by decades of experiments (ion gates, Rydberg and lattice simulators). Recognition could be timely after the 2022 and 2025 quantum-information prizes, but overlapping recognition is a risk.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 and 2022 prizes in quantum optics and information.
Many collaborators (Jaksch, Gardiner, Duan, Lukin) contributed to the foundational papers; I am relying on memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Current-induced spin-orbit torques allow switching of nanomagnets without external polarizers and are central to the physics of spin-orbit-coupled magnetic heterostructures and prospective memory technology. It ties quantum spin-orbit physics to practical use in the way I value, and it is where first-principles theory of interfaces matters.
assessment.attribution: Experimental credit to Miron/Gambardella (Rashba-type torques in Pt/Co/AlOx) and Buhrman (spin Hall torque switching) is plausible. Theoretical origins (Rashba, spin Hall effect theory, Manchon, Zhang and others) and the competing spin Hall versus Rashba interpretations complicate a fair trio.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and already in device development (SOT-MRAM), but the microscopic split between bulk spin Hall and interfacial contributions is not settled.
uncertainties: Unresolved competition between spin Hall and Rashba-Edelstein origins and allocation to the theorists of the spin Hall effect.
Nobel significance as physics versus device engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sub-picosecond demagnetization and all-optical switching revealed that magnetic order can be manipulated on timescales far below spin-lattice relaxation, a challenge for first-principles and spin-dynamics theory. It is a field in which I have personal expertise and so I weigh it with caution.
assessment.attribution: Beaurepaire's 1996 Ni experiment is the origin; Kimel and Rasing contributed all-optical switching and the 2007 helicity-dependent work. This credit split is reasonable, but Hohlfeld, Bigot and Stanciu's contributions may also be relevant.
assessment.maturity: Phenomenon confirmed in many materials and with XMCD/time-resolved spectroscopy, but the microscopic mechanism (spin-flip scattering, superdiffusive transport, light-induced currents) is still contested, which is a maturity concern.
uncertainties: Mechanism of ultrafast demagnetization still disputed.
My own research proximity may bias me; I try to compensate by ranking it below better-established discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reaching 10^-18 fractional uncertainty are an extraordinary precision-measurement achievement, enabling tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The concept of magic-wavelength trapping is original and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and Ye led the push to the lowest uncertainty; the pair is a clean configuration, but Hall (2005) recognized the comb that underpins them, and other groups (Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom, Yb) also reached similar accuracy.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmations by several groups worldwide; the redefinition of the second is pending, so a prize would be timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Credit for the measurement versus the idea.
Outside my core area; I defer on the AMO details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made single microwave photons interact with superconducting qubits in the strong-coupling regime, the foundation for readout and control in superconducting quantum processors. It is a quantum-device discovery with large downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf with Wallraff (not credited) are the key group; Wallraff's 2004 experiment is a conspicuous omission from the trio, which limits fairness of the proposed configuration.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across the entire superconducting-qubit community. After the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, a related award could be viewed as too close in time.
uncertainties: Wallraff's experimental role is not in the supplied credited names.
